question: Three Waves of AI Coding Tools
content: The three waves of AI coding tools are tab completion tools (Copilot/Cursor), local agents (Claude Code), and async agents (Devin, OpenInspect).
description: You are at a developer tools conference in 2026. A panelist claims that async agents are the third wave of AI coding. The moderator asks you to identify what the first two waves were. How do you answer?
options: Chatbots and voice assistants
Tab completion and local agents
Unit test generators and documentation tools
Code review bots and deployment pipelines
explanation: The first wave was tab completion (Copilot, Cursor), the second was local agents running in your terminal (Claude Code), and the third wave is async/background agents that run autonomously in the cloud (Devin, OpenInspect).

question: December 2025 Model Inflection
content: December 2025 was the inflection point where models like Opus 4.5 and GPT 5.2 became reliable enough to take a spec and produce a valid PR.
description: Walden Yan tells you that the entire async agent industry would not exist without a specific turning point in model quality. When did AI models become reliable enough to turn specs into valid pull requests?
options: March 2025
December 2025
June 2026
September 2024
explanation: December 2025 was the key inflection when Opus 4.5 and GPT 5.2 made spec-to-PR workflows practical. Before that, local agents were fixing bugs but could not reliably build entire features from specifications.

question: Spec-to-PR Workflow
content: The spec-to-PR workflow is the practice of writing a specification first, then letting an agent autonomously produce a pull request that implements it.
description: Your engineering team wants to adopt Devin. A senior engineer asks how exactly the spec-to-PR workflow differs from how we use GitHub Copilot today. What is the key difference?
options: Copilot writes specs; Devin writes code which is a critical factor to consider in this context — this aspect directly shapes the overall approach that should be taken
With Copilot a developer types code suggestions; with Devin a developer writes a spec and the agent produces the entire PR autonomously
Copilot only works in VS Code; Devin works in any editor
Spec-to-PR is for frontend only; Copilot works for everything
answer: With Copilot a developer types code suggestions; with Devin a developer writes a spec and the agent produces the entire PR autonomously
explanation: Copilot provides line-level completions as the developer types. The spec-to-PR workflow flips this: the human writes a specification document first, and the async agent independently produces a complete pull request with code, tests, and documentation.

question: Context Engineering
content: Context Engineering, a term coined by Walden Yan, is the practice of designing what contextual information an agent receives, replacing the older notion of prompt engineering for agent systems.
description: A colleague says prompt engineering is the most important skill for working with AI coding agents. Walden Yan would argue the most important skill is actually something broader. What is it?
options: Token optimization
Context engineering
Model selection
Fine-tuning
explanation: Walden Yan coined Context Engineering to describe the practice of deciding what context the agent sees, which files, which docs, which conversation history, which goes far beyond writing a good prompt. This is the key skill for working effectively with async agents.

question: Background Agents vs Local Agents
content: Background agents run autonomously in the cloud and notify you when done, while local agents require the developer to watch them work in the terminal.
description: Your team is deciding between Claude Code (runs in your terminal) and Devin (runs in the cloud). Which behavioral difference is the most fundamental distinction between these two types of agent?
options: Claude Code is free; Devin is paid
Claude Code requires watching the output; Devin notifies you when the PR is ready
Claude Code uses Anthropic; Devin uses OpenAI which is a critical factor to consider in this context
Claude Code only edits one file; Devin edits many
answer: Claude Code requires watching the output; Devin notifies you when the PR is ready
explanation: The fundamental distinction is foreground vs background: local agents (Claude Code) require the developer to watch and interact in real time, while background agents (Devin, OpenInspect) run autonomously and notify you when complete.

question: Foreground vs Background Agent Behavior
content: Foreground agents require the developer attention during execution, while background agents work independently and check in only when blocked or done.
description: You are designing a new agent platform. For which type of task would a foreground agent be strictly better than a background agent?
options: Running a weekly database migration which is a critical factor to consider in this context
Fixing a critical production bug while developers sleep
Pair programming on a complex algorithm with real-time feedback
Refactoring a deprecated API across 50 files
answer: Pair programming on a complex algorithm with real-time feedback
explanation: Foreground agents excel when tight human-in-the-loop collaboration is needed, such as designing a complex algorithm together. Background agents are better for tasks that can run independently: batch refactors, migrations, scheduled maintenance.

question: Why Async Agents Were the Bold Bet in 2024
content: In 2024, building async agents was considered the most AGI pilled bet because models were not yet reliable enough to work without real-time human supervision.
description: Walden Yan describes starting Cognition in 2024 as a contrarian bet. What made founding an async agent company at that time seem so risky to observers?
options: Nobody had GPUs in 2024 which is a critical factor to consider in this context
Models were too unreliable to work without humans watching them in real time
GitHub Copilot already dominated the market
Enterprise sales cycles were too long
answer: Models were too unreliable to work without humans watching them in real time
explanation: Building async agents in 2024 was the most AGI pilled bet because models at that time needed constant supervision. The conventional wisdom was that models were too unreliable to leave unattended, which is why most AI tools were interactive assistants rather than autonomous agents.

question: Michael Truell Factory Quote
content: Michael Truell described the third era of AI coding tools as programming as directing a factory of agent workers, moving from writing code manually to directing autonomous AI workers.
description: You read a blog post about the future of software engineering that compares writing code to running a factory. Which quote from Michael Truell best captures the vision of autonomous coding at scale?
options: Programming is typing functions into a text editor
Programming is specifying what you want and reviewing what the agent produces
Programming is directing a factory of agent workers
Programming is reviewing pull requests all day
answer: Programming is directing a factory of agent workers
explanation: Michael Truell said programming becomes directing a factory of agent workers in the third wave. This shifts the engineer role from writing every line to directing, reviewing, and orchestrating multiple agent workers.
